title: Stabilizer-preserving etale morphisms give cartesian moduli squares
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. Schemes, Deligne--Mumford stacks, representable morphisms and 2-fibre products have the meanings of [def-pc-scheme, def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], and algebraic spaces have the meaning of [def-trf-algebraic-space]. For a stack $\mathcal Y$, its inertia $I_{\mathcal Y}$ has objects $(y,\alpha)$ over a scheme $T$, where $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$ and $\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(y)$, and arrows $a:(y,\alpha)\to(z,\beta)$ satisfying $a\alpha=\beta a$. Its projection sends $(y,\alpha)$ to $y$. Finite inertia means that every scheme base change of this projection is a scheme finite over the base [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Let $h:\mathcal X_1\to\mathcal X_2$ be a representable-by-algebraic-spaces separated etale morphism of Deligne--Mumford stacks over $k$ with finite inertia. Assume that $I_{\mathcal X_1}\to\mathcal X_1\times_{\mathcal X_2}I_{\mathcal X_2}$ is an isomorphism. Let $p_j:\mathcal X_j\to M_j$ for $j=1,2$ be categorical moduli spaces over $k$: the $M_j$ are algebraic spaces over $k$, and composition gives a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_k(M_j,Z)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_k(\mathcal X_j,Z)$ for every algebraic space $Z/k$. Then the unique $k$-morphism $\bar h:M_1\to M_2$ satisfying $\bar h p_1=p_2h$ is separated etale, and the natural morphism $\mathcal X_1\to\mathcal X_2\times_{M_2}M_1$ is an equivalence of stacks. Etale is tested on scheme charts using [def-weil-etale-morphism]; separated for $h$ means proper relative diagonal [def-weil-proper-morphism], while separated for $\bar h$ means closed-immersion diagonal (closed immersion means locally a surjection on affine coordinate rings).

source.place: Tag 0DUV (lemma-etale-separated-over-keel-mori), restricted to Deligne--Mumford stacks over a field. Categorical moduli spaces are unique by their defining property, so the conclusion transports from the constructed moduli spaces to any categorical moduli spaces; the statement does not assume they already have flat-base-change compatibility.

proof.text: First the etale atlas of $\mathcal X_2$ is smooth by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], so [lem-sfb-etale-smooth-atlas-fppf-descent] makes it an algebraic stack in the source's fppf convention. By [lem-sfb-finite-inertia-etale-affine-charts] choose a small jointly surjective family $g_i:\mathcal A_i\to\mathcal X_2$ of separated etale stabilizer-preserving maps, with presentations $\mathcal A_i=[U_i/R_i]$ by affine finite locally free groupoids. Each $\mathcal A_i$ is DM: pull the atlas of $\mathcal X_2$ back along $g_i$ and refine the algebraic spaces by etale scheme atlases; [lem-sfb-dm-etale-atlas-calculus] supplies their compositions. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-flat-affine-groupoid-moduli] to the displayed presentations. It gives $f_i:\mathcal A_i\to B_i$ with $B_i$ affine, uniform categorical, quasi-compact, quasi-separated and a universal homeomorphism, and bijective on isomorphism classes over every algebraically closed extension. These are all the local vertical-map hypotheses of the gluing theorem used next. No finite-type hypothesis on $\mathcal X_2$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 0DUV (lemma-etale-separated-over-keel-mori), local comparison and descent argument

proof.text: Put $\mathcal A_{ij}=\mathcal A_i\times_{\mathcal X_2}\mathcal A_j$. Its projections are separated etale and stabilizer-preserving by the permanence clause of [lem-sfb-etale-stabilizer-preserving-affine-moduli]. Apply that node over $f_i$ to obtain a scheme $B_{ij}$, a uniform categorical map $f_{ij}:\mathcal A_{ij}\to B_{ij}$, and a cartesian square with separated etale $B_{ij}\to B_i$. Applying it over $f_j$ gives another categorical space; the two unique factorization maps are inverse because their composites with the categorical maps are identities. This identifies the two spaces and gives the second cartesian square $B_{ij}\to B_j$. Thus every overlap hypothesis of [lem-sfb-etale-local-moduli-gluing] holds. That node produces $q_2:\mathcal X_2\to Q_2$, an etale cover $B_i\to Q_2$, identifications $B_i\times_{Q_2}B_j=B_{ij}$, and cartesian squares $\mathcal A_i=\mathcal X_2\times_{Q_2}B_i$. Moreover $q_2$ is a universal homeomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0DUV (lemma-etale-separated-over-keel-mori), local comparison and descent argument

proof.text: The constructed $q_2$ is uniform categorical. For a flat $T\to Q_2$ and an algebraic space $Z/k$, a map $b:\mathcal X_2\times_{Q_2}T\to Z$ restricts over $T_i=T\times_{Q_2}B_i$ to a map from $\mathcal A_i\times_{B_i}T_i$. Uniform categoricality of $f_i$ gives a unique $c_i:T_i\to Z$. On $T_{ij}=T\times_{Q_2}B_{ij}$, the two restrictions have equal composites with the base change of $f_{ij}$, so are equal by its uniform categoricality [lem-sfb-etale-stabilizer-preserving-affine-moduli]. These applications are legitimate since $T_i\to B_i$ and $T_{ij}\to B_{ij}$ are base changes of the flat map $T\to Q_2$, by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. The $T_i$ cover $T$ etale by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. They glue the $c_i$ uniquely to $c:T\to Z$ because $Z$ is a sheaf [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The equality $c q_{2,T}=b$ and uniqueness hold on the same cover, hence globally. Here categoricality is proved, not inferred from the gluing node's statement.

source.place: Tag 0DUV (lemma-etale-separated-over-keel-mori), local comparison and descent argument

proof.text: Pull $h$ back to $\mathcal A_i$ and write $\mathcal C_i=\mathcal X_1\times_{\mathcal X_2}\mathcal A_i$. Its map to $\mathcal A_i$ is separated etale and stabilizer-preserving by [lem-sfb-etale-stabilizer-preserving-affine-moduli]; it is DM by [lem-sfb-dm-etale-atlas-calculus]. Apply [lem-sfb-affine-stack-stabilizer-etale-comparison] to $f_i$ and this map. Its hypotheses hold because $\mathcal A_i$ has a finite flat affine cover and $f_i$ is uniform categorical with affine target. Obtain a scheme $N_i$, a separated etale $N_i\to B_i$, and a cartesian equivalence $\mathcal C_i\simeq\mathcal A_i\times_{B_i}N_i$. The resulting $\mathcal C_i\to N_i$ is uniform categorical, since it is an etale, hence flat, base change of $f_i$ [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. The same assertion remains true after every flat base change of $N_i$.

source.place: Tag 0DUV (lemma-etale-separated-over-keel-mori), local comparison and descent argument

proof.text: Over $B_{ij}$ the two spaces $N_i\times_{B_i}B_{ij}$ and $B_{ij}\times_{B_j}N_j$ are categorical spaces for the same stack $\mathcal X_1\times_{\mathcal X_2}\mathcal A_{ij}$. Indeed the pullback equivalences from steps 2 and 4 identify both stack maps with the corresponding flat base changes of $\mathcal C_i\to N_i$ and $\mathcal C_j\to N_j$. Flatness follows because $B_{ij}\to B_i,B_j$ are etale [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. Unique factorization in both directions gives inverse isomorphisms $\theta_{ij}$ between the spaces. Each is over $B_{ij}$: the two structure maps have equal composites with the categorical map. On a triple overlap, both composites of these isomorphisms factor the same stack map, so uniqueness gives $\theta_{jk}\theta_{ij}=\theta_{ik}$; likewise $\theta_{ii}=1$. This is the cocycle calculation from the universal property, with no assertion that stabilizers are trivial.

source.place: Tag 0DUV (lemma-etale-separated-over-keel-mori), local comparison and descent argument

proof.text: Form $U=\coprod_iB_i$ and $V=\coprod_iN_i$ using [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] in the size bound of [def-weil-size-convention]. They are schemes, $U\to Q_2$ is a surjective etale map, and $V\to U$ is etale by the coproduct clause of [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. The $\theta_{ij}$ define descent data for this single cover: on the open-and-closed component $B_{ij}$ of $U\times_{Q_2}U$ use exactly $\theta_{ij}$. The cocycle of step 5 is the required cocycle on each triple component. Apply [lem-sfb-etale-space-single-cover-effective-descent] to obtain an algebraic space $Q_1$ and an etale map $u:Q_1\to Q_2$, with $Q_1\times_{Q_2}B_i\simeq N_i$. Only the singleton covering $\{U\to Q_2\}$ is used in that descent theorem.

source.place: Tag 0DUV (lemma-etale-separated-over-keel-mori), local comparison and descent argument

proof.text: The maps $\mathcal C_i\to N_i\to Q_1$ agree on overlaps by the construction of $\theta_{ij}$, and glue to $q_1:\mathcal X_1\to Q_1$ since $Q_1$ is a sheaf [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The covers here really are etale covers: $\mathcal C_i=\mathcal X_1\times_{Q_2}B_i$ and the family $B_i\to Q_2$ covers. Scheme refinements and their compositions are supplied by [lem-sfb-dm-etale-atlas-calculus]. The comparison $F:\mathcal X_1\to\mathcal X_2\times_{Q_2}Q_1$ restricts over $B_i$ to the equivalence of step 4. To check full faithfulness on a scheme test, restrict an isomorphism of images to this cover; the local equivalences give unique source isomorphisms, which agree and glue by the isomorphism-sheaf condition. For an object of the target, choose local preimages under those equivalences; their unique overlap isomorphisms satisfy the cocycle by full faithfulness and glue to an object by effective etale descent in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Thus $F$ is an equivalence, compatible with both projections.

source.place: Tag 0DUV (lemma-etale-separated-over-keel-mori), local comparison and descent argument

proof.text: Because $u$ is etale it is flat by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. The cartesian equivalence of step 7 makes $q_1$ a flat base change of $q_2$. For any further flat $T\to Q_1$, its composite to $Q_2$ is flat by the same node; the uniform categorical property proved in step 3 therefore proves uniform categoricality of $q_1$ as well. Both $q_1$ and $q_2$ are universal homeomorphisms: this holds for $q_2$ by step 2 and is preserved by base change simply because two successive base changes are one base change. In particular $\mathcal X_1\times_{\mathcal X_2}\mathcal X_1\simeq\mathcal X_2\times_{Q_2}(Q_1\times_{Q_2}Q_1)$ maps universally homeomorphically to $Q_1\times_{Q_2}Q_1$.

source.place: Tag 0DUV (lemma-etale-separated-over-keel-mori), local comparison and descent argument

proof.text: Consider the square with horizontal maps $\Delta_h:\mathcal X_1\to\mathcal X_1\times_{\mathcal X_2}\mathcal X_1$ and $\Delta_u:Q_1\to Q_1\times_{Q_2}Q_1$, and vertical maps from step 8. The top map is proper by the hypothesis that $h$ is separated, hence universally closed in the point-space sense of [def-sfb-dm-stack-morphism-properties]. After any algebraic-space base change $T\to Q_1\times_{Q_2}Q_1$, both vertical maps remain homeomorphisms. For a closed subset $C$ of the source of the bottom map, its inverse image under the left homeomorphism is closed; its image under the top map is closed; the right homeomorphism carries that image to precisely $\Delta_{u,T}(C)$ by commutativity and bijectivity of the vertical maps. Thus $\Delta_u$ is universally closed. By [lem-sfb-space-separated-diagonal-closed] it is a closed immersion. This proves separatedness of $u$ without any flat-base-change assertion about the originally given $p_j$.

source.place: Tag 0DUV (lemma-etale-separated-over-keel-mori), local comparison and descent argument

proof.text: Finally identify the constructed spaces with the spaces in the question. For $j=1,2$, categoricality of $q_j$ and $p_j$ gives unique maps $a_j:Q_j\to M_j$ and $b_j:M_j\to Q_j$ with $a_jq_j=p_j$ and $b_jp_j=q_j$. Then $(a_jb_j)p_j=p_j$ and $(b_ja_j)q_j=q_j$; injectivity in the respective universal properties gives $a_jb_j=1$ and $b_ja_j=1$. Thus $a_j$ is an isomorphism. The composite $a_2u b_1$ has composite $p_2h$ with $p_1$, hence is exactly $\bar h$ by its defining uniqueness. Isomorphisms identify its chart tests and diagonal with those of $u$, so it is separated etale. Under $a_1,a_2$ the functor of step 7 is precisely the natural comparison in the statement, because both its projections are $h$ and $p_1$. Therefore that comparison is an equivalence. All factorizations are over $k$, as required.
